title: Dizzy Dishes (Betty Boop's first appearance, Talkartoons)
studio: Fleischer Studios (dir. Dave Fleischer); Paramount Pictures
cut: 2:35-3:45 of the archive copy (70 s); scaled to 982x720 with light denoise to stay under 60 MB
contents: Waiter Bimbo forgets the gorilla's roast duck when he spots the singing poodle-girl on stage (the first-ever Betty Boop, still with dog ears), she sings 'I Have to Have You', he plays the roast duck like a saxophone and dances with her.
pd_us: US: PD since 1 Jan 2026 (released 9 Aug 1930; Wikipedia 'Dizzy Dishes': 'the short entered the US public domain on January 1, 2026'). Only Betty's 1930 dog-eared design is PD; her 1932+ human design remains copyrighted until those shorts expire.
pd_korea: Korea: PD. Korean Copyright Act Art. 42 protects cinematographic works for 70 years from publication (50 years before the 1 Jul 2013 amendment, which did not revive expired works); a film published in 1930 expired at the end of 2000 at the latest, so 1955-or-earlier films are PD. Korea's 1996 Berne restoration only covered foreign works still within the Korean term, so it does not apply.
trademark_caveat: BETTY BOOP is a live trademark of Fleischer Studios Inc. (licensed via King Features). Footage reuse fine; don't brand the channel or merchandise with her. Note: the source is a 1080p Blu-ray transfer of the U.M.&M. TV reissue print (its added 1950s title card, which is not in the cut, falsely claims 'Copyright MCMXXX by U.M.&M.'). A faithful transfer adds no new copyright in the US, and the cut contains no restoration credits.
